recipes.name: Cornbread Salad
ingredients_raw: 2 (11 ounce) cans whole kernel corn, drained

steps.text: To make the cornbread: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Spray the bottom and sides of an 8x8-inch pan with cooking spray.
Combine cornbread mix and water in a large mixing bowl until smooth; pour into prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, 30 to 35 minutes. Let cool; crumble and set aside.
Meanwhile, make the salad: Place bacon in a large skillet and cook over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until evenly browned, about 10 minutes. Drain bacon slices on paper towels.
Whisk sour cream, mayonnaise, and dressing mix together in a medium bowl.

Crumble 1/2 of the cornbread in the bottom of a large serving dish. Evenly layer with 1 can of pinto beans, 1/2 of the tomatoes, 1/2 cup green bell pepper, 1/2 cup green onions, 1 can of corn, 1 cup of cheese, 1/2 of the bacon, and 1/2 of the sour cream mixture. Repeat the layers. Cover and chill for at least 2 hours before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Cornbread Salad
raw_recipe.description: This layered cornbread salad is so flavorsome, thanks to the combination of tender cornbread, corn, tomatoes, bacon, cheese, and a creamy herb dressing.

video.description: Have you ever heard of a cornbread salad? It might sound strange, but it's easy to make, unique, and perfect for a party. In this video, Annie Campbell shows you how to make this delicious cornbread salad that combines cornbread, bacon, sour cream, mayonnaise, ranch dressing mix, pinto beans, tomatoes, green bell pepper, green onion, corn, and cheddar cheese.
video.name: How To Make Cornbread Salad

review.reviewBody: I use a large bottle of ranch dressing (any flavor) instead of mixing up the mayo, sour cream, and dry ranch.

It sounds really strange, but this is a great salad. I've made it twice. The first time I followed the recipe exactly, and I thought the mayonnaise taste was too strong. The second time I reduced the mayonnaise to one cup and found that to be just fine. There was enough dressing, even with that reduction. I also took some other reviewers suggestion and just mixed everything together. I was taking it to a parish picnic and thought it would be easier that way. I would probably do that again in the future. Some reviewers said they thought it was better the second day, but I did not. I thought it was a little too moist, probably because the juice from the tomatoes was released. I highly recommend this for a different and tasty salad.

This salad is a surefire showstopper and makes a stunning presentation when layered as the recipe suggests. I used a clear glass 6 quart trifle bowl and made a few adjustments, and it turned out perfectly. I used 2 packages of Jiffy cornbread mix prepared as to the package directions and added double the spices, as well as a 4 ounce can of chopped green chilis, and a finely chopped onion. I used black beans instead of pintos, and used 2 cans instead of one, and 2 cans of corn. I left the bacon amount the same, but doubled the dressing, onion, green pepper, green onion and tomato, and used 2 cups of cheese as the recipe states. Certainly, you can mix everything together as others have done, but if you're looking to impress a crowd, make the extra effort, and layer this salad. It was truly the star of the show at our church potluck, both in taste and presentation. This one is going straight into my favorite recipes box, and will be enjoyed again and again. The only mistake I made was not taking copies of the recipe, as it was requested over and over, and the rave reviews left me confident that I had indeed found a "keeper!"

This is always a hit at potlucks. I used Fleischmann's Simply Homemade cornbread mix, applewood bacon (which I doubled), corn off the cob, and orange peppers for color. It is best the next day, and to avoid getting soggy I de-seed the cherry tomatoes. I also add fresh chives as well. Simply yummy!

I will definitely make this again. I used black beans and pinto beans instead of all pinto beans. I also think Black Eyed Peas would work well. I made a recipe up of homemade ranch and added a little bit of sour cream to that and use that in the salad Because I felt it needed a little more liquid than what was mentioned plus I didn’t want all mayo. I used red onion because I only had one small bunch of green. It worked really well. I like the red onions and may use them exclusively next time. I also stirred it up because I forgot I was supposed to layer it! No problem, it all goes to the same place anyway. It looked lovely in the truffle bowl. I topped it with a bit of additional dressing and some cherry tomatoes. I also used Roma tomatoes rather than cherry tomatoes in the salad, which I Seeded and chopped. That avoided it being too soggy day one. However, it did get soggy overnight and it still tasted awesome; I think I liked it better that way! . Five people asked for the recipe and there were only a dozen there. It was a huge success.
I have made this for years. I add a sweet onion, instead of green, 16oz bottle of Ranch dressing, it’s delicious A big hit for any occasion.
Make this and love it. I change it up a little. I put a can of corn on top of the pintos and use pico de gallo instead of the chopped tomatoes. Always a hit wherever it is served!

This is absolutely the BEST cornbread salad recipe I have ever tasted! I did make a few MINOR changes. I used a skewer to poke some holes down into the salad and pour regular ranch dressing down into each of them. I still used the mayo, sour cream, and powdered ranch dressing mixture to layer into the salad. I also used one can of pinto beans and one can of kidney beans instead of TWO pintos. I do strongly recommend refrigerating this salad overnight instead of the recommended two hours. It makes the flavor so much better. My family LOVES this salad. I highly recommend it.
Love this! Makes a large bowl. The recipe left off that you're suppose to stir it up before you serve. Bottle dressing doesn't substitute well for the ranch packet mix.

I made this yesterday for a graduation party. I was a bit hesitant, since I had never heard of it! I used a loaf of plain and a loaf of jalapeno cornbread from the bakery. I substituted a can of black beans for one of the pintos. I used 4 ears of fresh sweet corn I cooked in the microwave, and instead of chopped tomatoes I used 2 packages of mini multicolored heirloom tomatoes. Also, instead of green pepper, I used red, yellow and orange peppers. I heard just now that it was a BIG HIT and I'm glad I made a small bowl for myself!

I make this salad a lot and everyone aloways loves it. The only difference in the recipe I have is that when you prepare the cornbread, you add one 4 oz. can of chopped green chilies and a little cumin to the batter. It just igves it a little bit of a kick. So delicious!

I love cornbread salad and this recipe is very spot on for the traditional kind made in the Appalachian Mountains where I live. I do have a question... The picture clearly shows only 1 layer of each with a little cornbread sprinkled on top... so why do the directions say to layer half of each and then repeat layers. Doing double layers is what I always do, but the recipe picture clearly only shows 1 layer of each.
Loved the flavor combination! Does great after setting in the fridge a few hours. Love the taste !!
This recipe looks good
Everyone at the party loved it.
My mom had never had cornbread salad, but she's a fan now. Followed exact recipe except I cut the ingredients by half because there are only two of us.
I'm going to make a small one since I am the only one in my little family who eats it. So good!
Definitely a keeper

My mom actually used to make this for every family functions. It was a good favorite, so much so she tried to switch it up one year and was asked to make this instead. There's only a few recipes that remind me of what an amazing cook my mom was and this one is definitely in the top 5.

I’d never had cornbread salad before, so I didn’t know what to expect, but the flavors worked together so well! My Texan husband approved and the kids even loved it (I wasn’t sure what they’d think of all the ingredients in the combo). The ranch dressing part was key to the flavor to me, so I wouldn’t skip that in favor of bottled ranch.
